{{Quote|What's to stop me from breaking your neck right now?''"<br />"''You could try, even if I didn't have a blaster, but I wouldn't advise it. I am stronger than you, and my heritage is&hellip; somewhat fiercer. Your chances of victory would be exceedingly small. Even with the knife and me barehanded, the odds are probably no better than fifty-fifty.|The criminal [[Mathal]] receives an anatomy lesson from his Sakiyan business partner, Tarnese Bleyd|<ref name="MS1">''[[MedStar I: Battle Surgeons]]''</ref>}}
The '''Sakiyans''' were a [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoid]] [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] [[Species/Legends|species]] whose anatomy featured slit-[[Eye/Legends|pupils]], pointed [[Ear/Legends|ears]], and [[Hair/Legends|hairless]] skin that varied in [[Color/Legends|shade]] from pale to jet black. Until the rise of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], [[Xenobiologist/Legends|xenobiologists]] had differing opinions as to whether Sakiyans should be classified as [[near-Human]]. However, internally, the species was vastly different from [[Human/Legends|Humans]] and related species. The Sakiyan [[Brain/Legends|brain]] was nearly twice the size of its Human equivalent, and the portions devoted to sensory input and processing were superior even to those in the brain of the [[Bith/Legends|Bith]] species. Sakiyans had incredible vision that extended into the [[Infrared/Legends|infrared]] spectrum, as well as highly acute and motion-sensitive peripheral vision. Sakiyan aural and olfactory senses were considered nearly supernatural by other species, as they allowed a Sakiyan to track and detect [[Standard day/Legends|days]]-old odors and faint noises. The species' musculature granted them 150 percent of the strength of a Human of equivalent size. Sakiyan [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-users]] were rare.

The species evolved from predatory animals on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Sakiya|Saki]] in [[Hutt Space/Legends|Hutt Space]]. Such ancestry endowed them with a love for the thrill and glory of [[Hunting/Legends|hunting]]. Because of this, Sakiyans were often employed as [[Assassin/Legends|assassins]] and [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunters]]. Sakiyans had a poor sense of humor and disliked being proven wrong. Honor was exceedingly important to members of the species, and they divided it into distinct types such as ''[[monthræl]]''&mdash;personal honor&mdash;and ''[[yithræl]]''&mdash;pride honor. After suffering personal dishonor, a Sakiyan's family and descendants were dishonored as well. However, a family member could lift the dishonor from the clan name through glory-bringing acts. Sakiyans tended to place the interests of themselves and their communities above those of others, and they were cautious in their dealings with other species, in part due to a succession of [[Alien/Legends|alien]] invasions of their [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]]. Members of the pale-skinned subspecies were treated as outcasts in Sakiyan society. Along with the [[Riileb (species)|Riileb]], the Sakiyans were one of the few Hutt Space species to resist conquest and invasion by the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutts]]. However, the Sakiyans did fall into an economic dependence on their [[The galaxy/Legends|galactic]] [[Gastropod/Legends|gastropod]] neighbors when the Hutts took controlling interests in Sakiyan technology companies that specialized in [[Repulsorlift/Legends|repulsorlift]] [[Engineer/Legends|engineering]]. The Sakiyans established colonies on worlds such as [[Sakidopa]], [[Sakiduba]], and [[Sakifwanna]].

==Biology and appearance==
{{Quote|This is a&mdash;whattayacallit&mdash;an ''outrage!"<br />"''This is how it ''is'', Naxy. If you think you're going to have free roam of the ''Mynock'', you better think again. I don't trust you. Until we find safe harbor, we're just gonna keep you safe and sound.''"<br />"''It reeks of gorg goo! Don't scum like you got any sense of smell?|Naxy Screeger demonstrates his species' keen senses to Cade Skywalker|<ref name="Leg23">[[Legacy (2006) 23|''Legacy'' (2006) 23]]</ref>}}
[[File:Djas_puhr.jpg|thumb|left|The large Sakiyan cranium housed a large brain with advanced capabilities to parse sensory input.]]
Sakiyans were [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoids]] who ranged in height from 1.6 to 2.1 [[Meter/Legends|meters]]. The [[Species/Legends|species]] was divided into both male and female [[Gender/Legends|sexes]], with dimorphism making the men taller than the women on average.<ref name="AA" /> Individuals had four<ref name="Hasbro DP" /> or five fingers per [[Limb/Legends|hand]], the digits capped by fingernails<ref name="Leg2">[[Legacy (2006) 2|''Legacy'' (2006) 2]]</ref> or claws.<ref name="MESM">{{StoryCite|story=My Enemies Surround Me!|book=Star Wars Weekly 106}}</ref> Each member of the species had a [[Skeleton/Legends|skeleton]] that included a spine<ref name="MS1" /> and cranium;<ref name="UAA" /> their bones contained [[marrow]].<ref name="LJ">[[The Last Jedi (novel)|''The Last Jedi'']]</ref> Tendons and ligaments connected bone to muscle at angles that made Sakiyans one and a half times as strong as a [[Human/Legends|Human]] of the equivalent size, and faster-moving as well. Ganglia of nerves lay under the flesh. Each Sakiyan also had a [[Heart/Legends|heart]],<ref name="MS1" /> whose pumping of [[Blood/Legends|blood]] escalated when a Sakiyan was excited, a condition detectable in the individual's pulse.<ref name="LJ" /> At least some members of the species were ambidextrous.<ref name="SWM:BH">{{SWMiniCite|set=Bounty Hunters|pack=Djas Puhr}}</ref>

Sakiyan skin was highly reflective,<ref name="CCG DP">{{CCG|set=Premiere Limited|cardname=Djas Puhr}}</ref> shining like burnished metal.<ref name="DMSH 22" /> Their skin [[Color/Legends|tones]] tended to be dark,<ref name="TGC">''[[Episode I Adventures 5: The Ghostling Children]]''</ref> ranging from pitch black to deep violet, red,<ref name="LECG" /> or green.<ref name="HFAS" /> However, lighter shades appeared as well, including gray,<ref name="Leg14" /> plum,<ref name="Sixtat Enc" /> bronze,<ref name="CNIII" /> jade,<ref name="PL" /> light blue,<ref name="SW29" /> and pink.<ref name="SWHS">''[[The Star Wars Holiday Special]]''</ref> The pale-skinned Sakiyans constituted a separate subspecies.<ref name="UAA" /> Sakiyan skin darkened when the individual flushed.<ref name="CNIII" /> Members of the species were resistant to extremes in temperature, able to operate comfortably&mdash;without breaking a sweat&mdash;at heat levels that might injure non-Sakiyans, as well as frigid depths, although those were less appealing to them. Sakiyans were able to use [[Synthflesh/Legends|synthflesh]] to heal wounded tissue. They were vulnerable to the effects of [[dendriton toxin]].<ref name="MS1" />

The shiny, [[Hair/Legends|hairless]] Sakiyan pate<ref name="UAA" /> left visible both subcutaneous veins<ref name="Hasbro DP" /> and the bifurcated cranium below,<ref name="SWHS" /> which was larger than that of a Human.<ref name="UAA" /> The expressive visage<ref name="MS1" /> was characterized by two [[Eye/Legends|eyes]], a [[Nose/Legends|nose]], and a [[Mouth/Legends|mouth]] with two [[Ear/Legends|ears]] on the sides. In some Sakiyans, the ears were pointed,<ref name="Hasbro DP" /> although those points were less pronounced in some members of the species<ref name="SW29" /> and completely absent in others. Facial structure varied such that some Sakiyans had prominent jowls<ref name="TWM">{{StoryCite|story=The Weapons Master!|book=Star Wars Weekly 104}}</ref> while others had svelte cheeks. Sakiyan eyes resembled those of Humans except that, whereas Human visual organs shrank to round pupils, the Sakiyans' narrowed to slits. Eye color varied less than that of Humans,<ref name="AA" /> with white,<ref name="MIBSW1">[[Star Wars (Marvel Illustrated Books)|''Star Wars'' (Marvel Illustrated Books)]]</ref> gray,<ref name="AA" /> silver,<ref name="Bounty" /> blue,<ref name="SWR49" /> yellow,<ref name="Brothers" /> and orange rimmed by red obtaining.<ref name="Sixtat Enc" /> In other specimens, the eye color changed depending on the lighting: one example had a red sclera, with irises that ranged from yellow<ref name="Leg2" /> to blue<ref name="Leg23" /> or green.<ref name="Leg2" /> [[Sinuses]] lay behind the nose, and those cavities were susceptible to burning from certain foods, such as [[ganno juice]].<ref name="HFAS" /> Sakiyans sported fangs<ref name="MS1" /> among their white [[Tooth/Legends|teeth]], which sprouted from pink gums.<ref name="CSWE III 131: NS">{{CSWECite|III|131|Naxy Screeger}}</ref> The depths of the Sakiyan throat could produce a low, rumbling noise, almost subsonic in nature,<ref name="MS1" /> and at least some members of the species had a gruff voice.<ref name="LJ" />

Because their appearance was so similar to that of the Human species, [[Xenobiologist/Legends|xenobiologists]] debated whether to classify the Sakiyans as a [[near-Human]] species or one completely [[Alien/Legends|unrelated]]. Those [[Scientist/Legends|scientists]] who argued for the latter status cited the species' vastly different [[Brain/Legends|brain]] structure as their strongest evidence. The brain was nearly double the size of its Human counterpart, a result of the organ's highly developed centers devoted to sensory input and reflexes. Indeed, the Sakiyans reached nearly supernatural levels of sensory perception, surpassing even the large-brained [[Bith/Legends|Bith]] in perceptual capabilities.<ref name="AA" /> Sakiyans enjoyed excellent visual acuity, with sight extending into the [[Infrared/Legends|infrared]] range and with keen peripheral vision.<ref name="CSWE III 124 Sa">{{CSWECite|III|124|Sakiyan}}</ref> Infrared light appeared as a silver glow to Sakiyan eyes, and their capability at detecting it allowed members of the species to even see through walls if adequate heat sources lay on the opposite side.<ref name="TGC" /> The wide variety of wavelengths to which their eyes were attuned made full-spectrum light seem almost like a glare to a Sakiyan,<ref name="MS1" /> even to the point of proving bothersome<ref name="TGC" /> and bringing tears to the eyes.<ref name="HFAS" /> The species' hearing was also well developed,<ref name="CSWE III 124 Sa" /> acute enough to detect a creature as tiny as a [[gravel-maggot]] burrowing through the soil.<ref name="HFAS" /> They enjoyed discriminatory smell, keen enough to track prey;<ref name="CSWE III 124 Sa" /> a skilled Sakiyan [[Hunting/Legends|hunter]] could smell the slightest trace of quarry, down to the smell of its sweat<ref name="MS1" /> or the after-odor of a recent [[Blaster/Legends|blaster]] [[Lightfight|fight]], and with a good whiff, a Sakiyan could detect a quarry's species and age.<ref name="TGC" /> In sum, the Sakiyan brain, evolved over centuries, gave them the senses and reflexes to be natural-born hunters.<ref name="MS1" />

Sakiyans entered adolescence at age 11 and reached full adulthood at age 16. They entered middle age at 49 and had a life expectancy of 85 [[Standard year/Legends|standard years]].<ref name="UAA" /> In advanced age, various Sakiyans suffered from dulled senses, with some even going deaf.<ref name="MS1" /> Possible physiological reactions to [[Death/Legends|dying]] included trembling and inability to focus the eyes.<ref name="LJ" /> Some members of the species exhibited [[Force-sensitive/Legends|sensitivity]] to [[The Force/Legends|the Force]], but the trait was generally rare among the Sakiyan population.<ref name="UAA" />

==Society and culture==
{{Quote|You're larger and much stronger, true, but I'm far faster. You are obviously adept with these ''[knives]'', but I still have the advantage.''"<br />"''You really think so? I'm a hunter and a warrior, bird-man, and I've killed half a dozen opponents with this very blade. You are fast, yes, but your bones are hollow and your feathers no protection against cold durasteel. No matter how fast you are, you can't get to me before I gut you.|The Nediji assassin Kaird faces off against his Sakiyan target, Tarnese Bleyd|<ref name="MS1" />}}
Sakiyan family structure separated the species into groups known as prides<ref name="MS1" /> or clans.<ref name="CNII" /> Each Sakiyan recognized an individual known as a [[pride-father]], and other individuals were known as [[pride elder]]s. The Sakiyans had highly developed concepts of honor that dictated how to respectfully treat others. Honor came in many varieties, each with its own distinct name and rules. ''[[Monthræl]]'' was a Sakiyan's personal honor, thought to also control the individual's destiny. ''[[Yithræl]]''&mdash;pride<ref name="MS1" /> or clan honor&mdash;was held in particularly high esteem. In the case of a clan's reputation being besmirched, the members might go to great length to redeem their collective honor;<ref name="CNII" /> indeed, piquing a Sakiyan's honor even caused physiological response, such as a racing pulse.<ref name="LJ" /> Obtaining large amounts of land or wealth was one means to do so. Sakiyan males were expected to provide for their families lest their personal and pride honor be diminished.<ref name="MS1" /> Sakiyans [[Marriage/Legends|wed]] to a mate,<ref name="CNIII" /> while the children were referred to as [[Youngling/Legends|younglings]]. Dying with a mark against one's honor was considered the cruelest fate that could befall a member of the species.<ref name="MS1" /> Sakiyans recognized special expanses called ''[[bonepit]]s''; seeing an [[Bird/Legends|avian]] [[Scavenger/Legends|scavenger]] known as a [[Flensor (species)|flensor]] fly over one's bonepit was considered an ill-omen.<ref name="CSWE I 280 Flensor">{{CSWECite|I|280|Flensor}}</ref> In Sakiyan religion, the afterlife was known as the [[Realm Beyond]].<ref name="MS1" />

[[File:Glocken_bites_the_dust.jpg|thumb|right|x150px|Sakiyans valued hunting prowess.]]
Clans were organized into convoluted family&ndash;[[Politics/Legends|political]] units.<ref name="MS1" /> On their [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] of [[Sakiya|Saki]],<ref name="EA" /> also known as Sakiya,<ref name="CA" /> these manifested as communities headed by selected leaders. The Sakiyans were a wary people who valued the survival and safety of their own community above those of others.<ref name="UAA" /> Coupled with a natural territoriality, especially when other hunters encroached on their domain,<ref name="MS1" /> they were cautious around outsiders&mdash;especially non-Sakiyans.<ref name="UAA" /> Their mantra was "survival demands efficiency."<ref name="MS1" /> Indeed, each settlement developed a detailed plan to enact in the event that an outside force attacked or attempted a conquest. To that end, communities maintained underground escape routes known as ''warrens''. Lightweight [[Repulsorlift/Legends|repulsorlift]] platforms lay in wait to evacuate children, the infirm, and important leaders, as well as to carry away important equipment and supplies in case of such danger. The Sakiyans were no pacifists, though: standing [[Army/Legends|armies]] responded to invading forces with tactics of harassment and retreat. Most invading forces gave up in the face of such resistance.<ref name="UAA" /> In a worst-case scenario, a Sakiyan had no compunction about eating other sentients, especially if family survival depended on such a decision.<ref name="MS1" /> Despite the wide variety of skin tones evident in the species, the Sakiyans ostracized their pale-skinned members as aberrations.<ref name="AA" />

Hunting was highly valued in Sakiyan society. While many Sakiyans practiced hunting on their homeworld, the species considered themselves self-assured predators in a [[The galaxy/Legends|galaxy]] replete with [[Grass/Legends|grass]]-[[Diet/Legends|eaters]] and only a few other predatory species worthy of Sakiyan respect.<ref name="MS1" /> They used not only their senses but also cunning,<ref name="CA" /> planning, and patience to capture prey;<ref name="MS1" /> for instance, when hunting for [[Gwayo bird/Legends|gwayo bird]] [[Egg/Legends|eggs]] on Saki, the hunter stalked the bird until led to its nest.<ref name="CA" /> Sakiyan hunters trained themselves to slow their heart rate and calm themselves; such measures allowed the individual to move with greater speed. Sakiyans also hunted for sport, with the more dangerous the quarry and the more perilous the hunt, the more honorable and satisfying it was to the hunter.<ref name="MS1" />

Saki was a [[Planet/Legends|planet]] abuzz with industrial activity,<ref name="EA" /> and Sakiyan technology was on par with other [[Realspace/Legends|spacefaring]] species.<ref name="UAA" /> An intelligent and hardy people,<ref name="EA" /> they particularly excelled at repulsorlift technology, with particular emphasis on the [[Engineer/Legends|engineering]] of components to be lighter and more efficient. For that reason, Sakiyan repulsorlift technology was highly sought after by the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutts]], which led the [[Gastropod/Legends|gastropod]] species to commission Sakiyan-designed [[Hoversled/Legends|repulsorsleds]] in ever more dainty and elaborate models. Hutt interests in Sakiyan repulsorlift engineering were so great that the Hutts virtually controlled the market, placing the Sakiyans into an ineluctable financial relationship with their [[Galaxy/Legends|galactic]] neighbors.<ref name="UAA" /> A variety of [[Unidentified Sakiyan flute|Sakiyan flute]] made a noise that members of the species found pleasant; the sound resembled a member of the [[Ghostling]] species sighing.<ref name="TGC" />

[[File:Ryn_Sakiyan_Sanyassan_Sarkan.jpg|thumb|left|A Sakiyan joined a Ryn and Sanyassan in a confrontation with a Sarkan.]]
At least some Sakiyans viewed other species as inferior due to their underdeveloped senses; in comparison to the Sakiyans, the belief went, other species could only hope to flail about in near blindness, lacking as they were in the ability to see into the infrared.<ref name="MS1" /> Still, some non-Sakiyans entered the tutelage of a Sakiyan hunter to improve their own hunting skills; the [[Nimbanel/Legends|Nimbanel]] [[Tawss Khaa/Legends|Tawss Khaa]] was one example.<ref name="CCG TK">{{CCG|set=Special Edition Limited|cardname=Tawss Khaa}}</ref> Because full-spectrum light bothered them, Sakiyans in the galaxy at large coped by wearing [[Glareshades|dark visors]] in bright light<ref name="HFAS" /> or dimming room lighting to avoid glare.<ref name="MS1" /> Typical Sakiyan clothing included elaborate robes<ref name="UAA" /> or full-body [[Jumpsuit/Legends|jumpsuits]]. At least some Sakiyans sported facial markings.<ref name="Sixtat Enc" /> Sakiyans disliked being doubted and even less being shown to be wrong. They were not entirely fearless;<ref name="LJ" /> for instance, one Sakiyan joined a Ryn and a Sanyassan in keeping a safe distance from a Sarkan.<ref name="UAA" />

Sakiyans expressed emotion through their faces; a frown indicated discomfort, while a smile indicated pleasure.<ref name="MS1" /> Although able to laugh,<ref name="LJ" /> Sakiyans were not known for their well-developed senses of humor.<ref name="UAA" /> Raising two hands and shaking the head conveyed that the Sakiyan recognized his or her interlocutor's attempt at trickery, while rolling the eyes indicated annoyance.<ref name="PP">{{Wizards|url=default.asp?x=starwars/livingforce/swlf20040603|text=Political Platforms}}</ref> Another gesture was to snap fingers when struck by an idea, and to shrug to indicate disinterest<ref name="CNIII" /> or self-deprecation.<ref name="MS1" /> A snort indicated derision,<ref name="CNIII" /> while a growl denoted anger.<ref name="MS1" /> Anticipation might cause a Sakiyan to tremble.<ref name="LJ" /> Their native [[Language/Legends|language]] was also known as [[Sakiyan (language)|Sakiyan]],<ref name="LECG" /> which the typical member of the species could both speak and write.<ref name="AA" /> They could also speak [[Galactic Basic Standard/Legends|Basic]],<ref name="LECG" /> and many learned [[Huttese/Legends|Huttese]] as well. Sakiyan names consisted of two parts, a clan name followed by a personal name; for instance, the Sakiyans [[Tarnese Bleyd]] and [[Tarnese Lyanne]] both came from [[Clan Tarnese]].<ref name="MS1" /> Other examples of names included Ejaf Ya-Drun, Johr Penyk, Djas Puhr, Kol Rzad, Tuden Sal, Moja Skunaz, and Vihn Thas.<ref name="UAA" /> The clan name doubled as a Sakiyan's personal [[Blood/Legends|blood]] cry.<ref name="MS1" />

==History==
{{Quote|My people's ancestors were warriors, but they can't match&mdash;no one in the galaxy can&mdash;humans for sheer bloodthirstiness.|Tuden Sal|<ref name="CNIII">''[[Coruscant Nights III: Patterns of Force]]''</ref>}}
[[File:Sakiyan_servant_for_a_Hutt.jpg|thumb|right|The Sakiyans had a millennia-long relationship with the Hutts.]]
The tropical world of Saki,<ref name="UAA" /> in [[Orbit/Legends|orbit]] around the [[Star/Legends|star]] [[Saki Prime]],<ref name="MS1" /> served as the backdrop for the evolution of the Sakiyan species.<ref name="UAA" /> The planet's little seasonal variation gave rise to wide swaths of jungles, [[Swamp/Legends|swamps]], and veldts punctuated by savannas and lakes.<ref name="MS1" /> The species' ancestors were prey animals<ref name="LECG" /> who dwelt in [[Tree/Legends|trees]] and atop natural high points.<ref name="MS1" /> As a response to the dangerous predators of their world, the early Sakiyans evolved advanced senses as a survival mechanism.<ref name="UAA" /> Eventually, the Sakiyans themselves developed into a species of successful hunters, their senses honed to track prey, and sporting dark skin to camouflage them against the backdrop of their homeworld.<ref name="TGC" /> Based on their highly developed brains, xenobiologists postulated that the earliest Sakiyans arose far back in the galactic past.<ref name="AA" /> As the species developed the capacity to use tools and create their own shelter, they maintained their advanced senses, unlike countless other species.<ref name="UAA" /> Meanwhile, generations spent as hunters made the Sakiyans tough and durable.<ref name="MS1" />

From at least [[25,000 BBY/Legends|25,000 BBY]],<ref name="EA" /> the Sakiyans faced numerous invasions by offworlders intent on conquering their planet.<ref name="AA" /> Due to their homeworld's location in the ''[[Bootana Hutta/Legends|Bootana Hutta]]'',<ref name="EA" /> close to [[Hutt Space/Legends|Hutt Space's]] [[Astrography|astrographical]] center, the species came into contact with the Hutts in the distant past.<ref name="UAA" /> Indeed, Sakiyan records were some of the oldest to chronicle the early spacefaring civilization of the Hutts, telling of "Hutt cavaliers" in [[Armor/Legends|armor]]&mdash;sometimes speculated to have been precursors to the [[Shell Hutts]]&mdash;and recording Sakiyan tribute sent to the Hutts, including technological expertise in the form of help with developing ''[[planechanga]]'', enormous railguns able to propel boulders through space at such speeds that they could crack a planet upon impact.<ref name="EGW">''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]''</ref> The Sakiyans were careful to keep the Hutts at a distance in all aspects of life on Saki save commerce; in this way, the Hutts were wooed into settling for economic domain over Saki and its denizens rather than outright political control,<ref name="UAA" /> a feat only bested by the [[Riileb (species)|Riileb]] of the planet [[Riileb/Legends|Riileb]], who evaded even economic control by the Hutts.<ref name="AE">''[[Alien Encounters]]''</ref> The arrangement allowed the Sakiyans to avoid becoming an [[Slavery/Legends|enslaved]] species, as was the fate of most other non-Hutt natives of Hutt Space<ref name="UAA" />&mdash;although at least one [[Unidentified Sakiyan|Sakiyan]] did serve the Hutts in some capacity.<ref name="EA" /> Instead the Sakiyans remained independent and respected by their Hutt neighbors.<ref name="EGW" /> Relations remained fraught between the two species for millennia,<ref name="EA" /> with the Sakiyans referring to their neighbors as "slugs."<ref name="UAA" />

Other invasion attempts were made by the [[Tion Hegemony/Legends|Tion Hegemony]], the [[Sith/Legends|Sith]], and the [[Drackmarian]]s.<ref name="AA" /> As the Tionese expanded under the reign of [[Xim/Legends|Xim the Despot]], the Sakiyans had already established their relationship with the Hutts. When the Tionese encountered Sakiyan and Nimbanese [[Merchant/Legends|traders]] who claimed to serve the Hutts, Xim's curiosity was piqued, prompting his [[Xim Wars|war]] with the Hutts.<ref name="XW">{{SW|url=news/essential-atlas-extra-the-history-of-xim-and-the-tion-cluster|text=Essential Atlas Extra: The History of Xim and the Tion Cluster|int=Xim Week: The History of Xim and the Tion Cluster}}</ref> The Sakiyan homeworld later fell within the bounds of [[Sith Worlds/Legends|Sith Space]] from [[1004 BBY|1004]] to [[1000 BBY/Legends|1000 BBY]], during the [[New Sith Wars]].<ref name="EA" /> Xenobiologists postulated that as a result of those hostile encounters with outsiders, the Sakiyans developed their propensity for caution and mobility in their communities.<ref name="AA" />

At some point, the Sakiyans received peaceful visitors from the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]], [[Scout/Legends|scouts]], who shared with the species the secrets of repulsorlift technology. The Sakiyans recognized the possibilities that repulsorlift afforded them in their efforts to remain deft and mobile, and their engineers tweaked the technology to emphasize those attributes. Their efforts came to the attention of the Hutts, who soon established their economic dominance over the Sakiyan repulsorlift industry.<ref name="UAA" /> The Sakiyans were represented in the Galactic Republic by [[Senator/Legends|senators]].<ref name="MS1" /> They eventually founded three colony worlds, [[Sakidopa]], [[Sakiduba]], and [[Sakifwanna]], each located in a [[Star system/Legends|star system]] of the same name.<ref name="EA" />

After the rise of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]]<ref name="AA" /> in [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]],<ref name="NEC 73" /> the Sakiyan homeworld's location in the bowels of Hutt Space kept the species insulated from the grasp of [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] and his forces. However, the Empire abducted Sakiyan [[Technician/Legends|technicians]] and forced them to work in Imperial research and development centers to improve the Empire's repulsorlift technology, particularly in the development of new [[Hovertank/Legends|repulsortanks]]. During that period, xenobiologists finally settled the debate over whether to classify the Sakiyans as near-Humans or non-Human, coming to the consensus that the Sakiyans were non-Human based both on their appearance and the vast differences in their brain structure.<ref name="AA" />

With the fall of the Empire and the rise of the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]]<ref name="UAA" /> in [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]],<ref name="NEC 73" /> both that new government and the [[Hapan]]s<ref name="UAA" /> of the [[Hapes Consortium/Legends|Hapes Consortium]]<ref name="CSWE II 16">{{CSWECite|II|16|Hapes Consortium}}</ref> approached the Sakiyans to broker political and commercial alliances. Nevertheless, the Sakiyans remained wary, telling the outsiders to speak to the Hutts instead. After the species known as the [[Yuuzhan Vong]] made their first advance on Hutt Space<ref name="UAA" /> in [[26 ABY/Legends|26 ABY]]<ref name="NEC 73" /> during their [[Yuuzhan Vong War|invasion]] of the galaxy, they spared the [[Saki system/Legends|Saki system]]. The unorthodox tactics of the alien invaders worried the Sakiyan leadership that the outsiders might be able to circumvent the Sakiyans' battle-tested strategies to resist invasion. They thus began to make furtive overtures of support to the New Republic and the Hapans in the case those groups decided to counterattack the Yuuzhan Vong.<ref name="UAA" /> After the Yuuzhan Vong devastated Hutt Space, the fate of the Sakiyans remained unknown to the rest of the galaxy. By circa [[25 ABY/Legends|25 ABY]], the population of the Saki system was between 100 to 500 million inhabitants.<ref name="EA" />

==Sakiyans in the galaxy==
{{Quote|Thorp! Thorp, after all I've done for you&hellip; Short memory, eh, Thorp? ''Short memory!|Ackmena reacts to the refusal of her Sakiyan patron, Thorp, to leave her cantina|<ref name="SWHS" />}}
[[File:Sakiyan_vs_Savage.png|thumb|left|x150px|Some Sakiyans held mundane jobs, such as cargo hauling.]]
Sakiyans rarely ventured away from their home system,<ref name="UAA" /> let alone away from what they considered the ideal conditions of their homeworld proper.<ref name="MS1" /> They generally lacked the inclination to trade with outsiders. The same attitudes prevailed on the few Sakiyan colony worlds.<ref name="UAA" /> Still, Sakiyans could be found off Sakiyan planets in small numbers, making them not uncommon sights in areas where beings of diverse species and background congregated.<ref name="DMSH 22" /> For example, in [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]],<ref name="NEC 73" /> a [[Unidentified Sakiyan inn patron|Sakiyan]] with a heavily scarred head was present at the [[Dewback Inn]] on the planet [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] when the Human clerk [[Lorn Pavan]] and his [[Droid/Legends|droid]] [[I-5YQ]] visited the establishment.<ref name="DMSH 22" /> Another Sakiyan was present at a [[Cantina/Legends|cantina]] in the [[City/Legends|city]] [[Mos Espa/Legends|Mos Espa]] on the planet [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]]<ref name="EI05">[[Episode I: The Phantom Menace ½|''Episode I: The Phantom Menace'' ½]]</ref> that same year<ref name="NEC 73" /> while the [[Devlikk/Legends|Devlikk]] [[Podracer (profession)/Legends|Podracer]] [[Wan Sandage/Legends|Wan Sandage]] negotiated to have the [[Glymphid/Legends|Glymphid]] [[Assassin/Legends|assassin]] [[Aldar Beedo/Legends|Aldar Beedo]] kill the [[Dug/Legends|Dug]] racing champion [[Sebulba/Legends|Sebulba]].<ref name="EI05" /> Likewise, a short [[Time/Legends|time]] after the [[First Battle of Geonosis/Legends|Battle of Geonosis]] in [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]],<ref name="NEC 73" /> a [[Unidentified Sakiyan spacer|Sakiyan]] was present on [[The Wheel/Legends|the Wheel]] [[Space station/Legends|space station]] when the [[Twi'lek/Legends|Twi'lek]] [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Aayla Secura/Legends|Aayla Secura]] searched for her missing [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]], the [[Kiffar/Legends|Kiffar]] [[Quinlan Vos/Legends|Quinlan Vos]].<ref name="SWR49" /> Later in the same period, a male Sakiyan was present in a bar on Tatooine when his companion, a [[Unidentified tentacle-faced species/Legends|non-Human]] named [[Oked/Legends|Oked]], crossed the [[Dathomirian/Legends|Dathomirian]] [[Asajj Ventress/Legends|Asajj Ventress]]&mdash;and paid with his life.<ref name="Bounty" /> After the end of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] and the rise of the Galactic Empire in 19 BBY, another [[Unidentified Sakiyan restaurant patron|Sakiyan]] was eating [[nexufish]] [[sulyet]] at [[Gort's]], a restaurant on Coruscant, when the Human Jedi [[Jax Pavan]] and the [[Korun/Legends|Korun]] [[Soldier/Legends|soldier]] [[Nick Rostu]] patronized the establishment. Later that year, a [[Unidentified eye-patch-wearing Sakiyan|Sakiyan]] with an [[Eye patch/Legends|eye patch]] hustled to get out of the way of [[Prince/Legends|Prince]] [[Xizor/Legends|Xizor]] of Black Sun in the [[Yaam Sector]] of Coruscant.<ref name="CNI" /> [[Thorp]] was a pale-skinned Sakiyan<ref name="CRC 2">{{SWArchive|url=episode-iv/bts/article/f20030502/index.html|text=Cantina Roll-Call: Shedding Light on Some Alien Aliases|int=Cantina Roll-Call: Shedding Light on Some Alien Aliases}}</ref> active after the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]] in [[0 ABY/Legends|0 ABY]]. By that time, he had come to owe [[Ackmena/Legends|Ackmena]], the Human [[Bartender/Legends|bartender]] of the [[Chalmun's Spaceport Cantina/Legends|Mos Eisley Cantina]], a favor. When the Empire established a curfew on Tatooine on a night that Ackmena was on duty, the Sakiyan ignored the bartender's pleas for the patrons to go home, even starting a round of jeering to demand more [[Alcohol/Legends|drinks]]. Intoxicated, he eventually stumbled out, ushered along by Ackmena and her [[bouncer]], [[Tork]].<ref name="SWHS" />

For employment, Sakiyans at large often operated as [[Noble/Legends|nobles]] and scouts,<ref name="UAA" /> or held more mundane positions in galactic society. For example, circa [[20 BBY/Legends|20 BBY]],<ref name="date">The ''[[Living Force Campaign Guide]]'' states that the [[Living Force (roleplaying campaign)|''Living Force'']] campaign is set one [[Standard year/Legends|year]] after the [[Invasion of Naboo/Legends|Invasion of Naboo]], an event that is dated to [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]] by ''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''. As the ''Living Force'' adventure "[[Below the Belt: Philology]]" [[Cularin's disappearance|moved]] the campaign forward ten years to the [[Time/Legends|time]] of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], and the adventure "[[Night Eyes: Night's Homecomin]]" established that by Year 4 of the campaign over a year had elapsed since the events of ''Philology'', "[[Political Platforms]]" can therefore be dated to circa [[20 BBY/Legends|20 BBY]].</ref> the Sakiyan [[Brug D'Shar]] served as the aide-de-camp to the Human Counselor [[Westa Impeveri]] on the planet [[Cularin/Legends|Cularin]], a position that earned him a reputation for electoral fraud. As a panelist during a meeting moderated by Human [[Journalist/Legends|reporter]] [[Yara Grugara]], Brug advocated the use of [[Platform city|platform cities]] on Cularin because they benefitted the economy and helped deter overcrowding.<ref name="PP" /> [[Vadoo/Legends|Vadoo]] was a young Sakiyan captured by [[Trandoshan/Legends|Trandoshan]] hunters and brought to the [[Moon/Legends|moon]] [[Wasskah/Legends|Wasskah]] to be hunted for sport during the Clone Wars.<ref name="CWEG:PL">{{SWArchive|url=theclonewars/guide/episode321.html|text=''The Clone Wars'' Episode Guide: Padawan Lost}}</ref> Vadoo was killed by the Trandoshans after arrival, as the hunters opened fire with their [[Vermin-Thrax/Legends|ship's]] [[Laser cannon/Legends|laser cannons]] to identify the most worthy target for their hunt.<ref name="PL" /> A male [[Unidentified Sakiyan cargo hauler/Legends|Sakiyan cargo hauler]] was present on the planet [[Stobar/Legends|Stobar]] near a restaurant called [[Plop Dribble's/Legends|Plop Dribble's]] during the same war when the [[Zabrak/Legends|Zabrak]] [[Nightbrothers/Legends|Nightbrother]] [[Savage Opress/Legends|Savage Opress]] demanded that he take him to the planet [[Lotho Minor/Legends|Lotho Minor]]. Upon arrival, Opress kicked the [[Pilot/Legends|pilot]] out of the [[Starship/Legends|starship]] to plummet to the surface of the planet.<ref name="Brothers" /> [[Finn (bartender)|Finn]] was a Sakiyan bartender at a tavern called [[Rik's Cantina/Legends|Rik's]] circa [[137 ABY]];<ref name="Leg14" /> in addition to mixology, he was a competent fighter&mdash;skills that allowed him to act not only as the chief bartender but as an enforcer as well.<ref name="CSWE I 273: Finn">{{CSWECite|I|273|Finn}}</ref>

Sakiyans made talented scientists and engineers. Members of the species were especially common in repulsorlift engineering and development.<ref name="AA" /> During the Clone Wars, a [[Unidentified Sakiyan scientist|Sakiyan scientist]] found work as a contractor for the company [[Arkanian Microtechnologies]]. She participated in a project to [[Re-engineering|re-engineer]] animals, a process that rendered its subjects stronger and more docile. However, she made enemies who placed a [[Bounty/Legends|bounty]] on her head, so she thus became the target of a [[Gand/Legends|Gand]] [[Findsman/Legends|Findsman]] named [[Vaskau Farg]]&mdash;who viewed her not as a researcher but as a "[[Witch/Legends|witch]]." The Sakiyan traveled to the planet [[Arkania/Legends|Arkania]], where she bought a [[Speeder/Legends|speeder]] in the settlement of [[Novania]] and headed off into the tundra to an [[Unidentified Arkanian Microtechnologies installation|Arkanian Microtechnologies installation]]. Farg tracked her with his Force abilities and confronted her there.<ref name="AC">{{Wizards|url=default.asp?x=starwars/article/sw20030206arkanianintro|text=Arkanian Chill|int=Arkanian Chill}}</ref> Later, under the regime of the Galactic Empire, Sakiyans were forcibly removed from their homeworld to toil in such facilities for the Empire.<ref name="AA" />

===Hunters and prey===
{{Quote|I smell blaster fire. What's going on? Why the security alert?''"<br />"''Intruders. I found them messing with our slaves. I took a shot at them.''"<br />"''What kind of intruders?''"<br />"''Small creatures, wearing hooded robes. They might have been Jawas.''"<br />"''Not Jawas. Humans. I smell human children.|Sakiyan bounty hunter Djas Puhr corrects his Dug partner, [[Khiss (Dug)|Khiss]]|<ref name="TGC" />}}
Many offworld Sakiyans found work as assassins, an occupation in which their keen senses gave them an advantage over their competitors. Similarly, keen senses made Sakiyans apt [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunters]] as well.<ref name="SWE">''[[Star Wars Encyclopedia]]''</ref> An example was [[Djas Puhr/Legends|Djas Puhr]],<ref name="Hasbro DP" /> who, in 32 BBY,<ref name="Kitster DB">{{DB|character|kitster|Banai, Kitster}}</ref> was one of several Sakiyans working for the Dug Podracer Sebulba<ref name="DB Sebulba">{{DB|character|sebulba|Sebulba}}</ref><ref name="NEGC">''[[The New Essential Guide to Characters]]''</ref> to capture luckless victims to sell as slaves while the Dug took part in [[Podracing/Legends|Podraces]]<ref name="TGC" /> in the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]].<ref name="NEGC" /> On one occasion, Djas led an expedition to the planet [[Datar/Legends|Datar]] to collect Ghostling children from their [[Unidentified Ghostling village|nests]]. After being transported to the [[Desert/Legends|desert]] planet [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]], the children escaped with the aid of the Human child [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]],<ref name="TGC" /> so Sebulba tasked Djas with recapturing them.<ref name="CSWE III 49: DP">{{CSWECite|III|49|Djas Puhr}}</ref> The Sakiyan also hoped to nab the Human boy and his companions to claim a bounty placed on them by [[Gardulla Besadii the Elder/Legends|Gardulla the Hutt]]. Nevertheless, the children evaded capture again and again,<ref name="HFAS" /> eventually seeking refuge in the [[Gardulla's pleasure garden|pleasure garden]] of [[Imperial Station Bravo|Gardulla's fortress]]. When the Ghostling Princess [[Arawynne]] escaped the bounty hunter's pursuit with the help of a [[Wistie/Legends|Wistie]] [[Unidentified Wistie (Arawynne's lookout)|lookout]], Djas deduced that the Ghostlings and their allies intended to escape through the [[Garden/Legends|garden's]] ventilation system. Djas homed in on the would-be escape vent and covered the garden side while Sebulba blocked the exterior exit. The ploy worked; Djas recaptured the children,<ref name="CA" /> who were then scheduled for execution in the [[Mos Espa Grand Arena/Legends|Mos Espa Grand Arena]]. Nevertheless, Djas was forced to track the slaves down once again when they escaped the arena and fled to a natural formation called [[Bantha Rock]]. By the time he arrived with Sebulba and his [[Abyssin/Legends|Abyssin]] partner [[Gondry]], the quarry of Ghostlings had already been evacuated from Tatooine.<ref name="TOT">''[[Episode I Adventures 8: Trouble on Tatooine]]''</ref>

[[File:Myo_Muftak_Lirin_Djas.jpg|thumb|left|Djas Puhr was a bounty hunter active during the Galactic Civil War.]]
Djas remained an active bounty hunter for decades. By [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]], he had developed a reputation as an imposing figure who followed through on his promises.<ref name="FF CAN6">{{FactFile|22|CAN 1-6|Mos Eisley Cantina Characters}}</ref> As a regular fixture of the Mos Eisley Cantina on Tatooine, he kept to the shadows, watched the denizens of [[Mos Eisley/Legends|Mos Eisley]] go about their business,<ref name="SWM:BH" /> gathered information, and sought out bounties to hunt.<ref name="Hasbro DP" /> The process worked; Djas was highly sought after by the later stages of his career,<ref name="FF CAN6" /> even earning contracts from [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure/Legends|Jabba the Hutt]].<ref name="CVD">''[[Star Wars: The Complete Visual Dictionary]]''</ref> Djas sat at a table with the [[Talz/Legends|Talz]]'' drifter [[Muftak/Legends|Muftak]], the Abyssin scout [[Myo/Legends|Myo]], and the [[Bith/Legends|Bith]]'' [[Musician/Legends|musician]] [[Lirin Car'n/Legends|Lirin Car'n]]<ref name="BTM">''[[Star Wars: Behind the Magic]]''</ref> on the [[Standard day/Legends|day]] that the Humans [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]], a Jedi Master, and [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]], a [[Moisture farmer/Legends|moisture farmer]], met the [[Corellian/Legends|Corellian]] [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggler]] [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]] and his [[Wookiee/Legends|Wookiee]] co-pilot [[Chewbacca/Legends|Chewbacca]].<ref name="ANH">{{Film|IV}}</ref> [[File:SixtatHS-SWE.png|thumb|right|upright|Sixtat was a Sakiyan bounty hunter active during the Clone Wars.]]Another bounty hunter and a contemporary of Djas's was [[Sixtat/Legends|Sixtat]]. The Sakiyan, also known as the Outlands Butcher,<ref name="TB">{{TCW|The Box}}</ref> became infamous for his skills as a hunter, which led him to become supercilious and overconfident.<ref name="Sixtat Enc" /> His renown was so great that during the Clone Wars, the [[Head of State/Legends|Head of State]] of the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]], [[Count/Legends|Count]] [[Dooku/Legends|Dooku]], chose Sixtat as one of twelve bounty hunters to take on [[the Box]], a death machine invented by the [[Phindian/Legends|Phindian]] criminal [[Moralo Eval/Legends|Moralo Eval]]. The last few surviving hunters would earn themselves a lucrative contract: to kidnap Palpatine, [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] of the Galactic Republic. Sixtat fought through a succession of challenges alongside his competition and survived to face the final test: firing a [[Sniper rifle/Legends|sniper rifle]] to hit three small, moving targets. Sixtat made his first two shots, but he missed on his third; the blunder caused the ground to retract from below him, and he plunged to his death in a pit of [[Fire/Legends|fire]].<ref name="TB" />

Sakiyan soldiers<ref name="UAA" /> found employment in military<ref name="MS1" /> and [[Bodyguard/Legends|bodyguard]] posts.<ref name="TT 5">{{Wizards|url=default.asp?x=starwars/article/sw20040122threat|text=Triplet Threat|int=Triplet Threat}}</ref> In [[20 BBY/Legends|20 BBY]], during the Clone Wars, the Sakiyan Tarnese Bleyd served as an [[Admiral/Legends|admiral]] in the [[Republic Navy/Legends|Republic Navy]], posted as the commanding [[Officer/Legends|officer]] of ''[[MedStar Nineteen]]'', a [[MedStar-class frigate/Legends|''MedStar''-class medical frigate]] stationed at [[Drongar/Legends|Drongar]].<ref name="NEC 73">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref> Reeling from his clan's misfortunes when his pride-father, Tarnese Lyanne, was betrayed by underworld business partners in the [[Black Sun/Legends|Black Sun]] criminal organization, and resentful of what he considered a backwater assignment, Tarnese entered an arrangement with [[Filba]] the Hutt of Black Sun<ref name="MS1" /> to steal a medical substance known as [[Bota/Legends|bota]] from the [[Frigate/Legends|frigate]].<ref name="NEC 73" /> Tarnese hoped both to restore his clan's prestige through the new wealth but also eventually to double-cross his Black Sun contacts as retaliation for what they had done to his pride-father.<ref name="CSWE I 79: TB">{{CSWECite|I|79|Bleyd, Tarnese}}</ref> During his dealings with the underworld, Tarnese made a sport of hunting down and killing Black Sun operatives who attempted to strong-arm him. However, when a [[Sullustan/Legends|Sullustan]] reporter named [[Den Dhur]] overheard Tarnese meeting with Filba, the Admiral knew the jig was up and attempted to pin the operation on his Hutt partner. Black Sun sent a [[Nediji]] assassin named [[Kaird]] to kill Tarnese instead. The Sakiyan put up a fierce fight in the ensuing [[Knife/Legends|knife]] battle, but the Nediji used [[dendriton toxin]]&mdash;a dishonorable move in the Sakiyan's eyes&mdash;to gain the advantage and slay the Sakiyan.<ref name="MS1" />

In 19 BBY,<ref name="CN2 p">''[[Coruscant Nights II: Street of Shadows]]'', Prologue</ref> a [[Unidentified Sakiyan bouncer|Sakiyan]] worked as the bouncer at [[Quarek'k]], a rough-and-tumble establishment in the [[Coruscant Underworld/Legends|underlevels]] of Coruscant.<ref name="CNII" /> In 0 ABY,<ref name="NEC 73" /> the Sakiyan [[Glocken]] worked as an enforcer for an old, Human cantina owner named [[Merl]] in the spaceport city [[Muracie]] on the planet [[Centares/Legends|Centares]].<ref name="TT 5" /> When the bounty hunter [[Beilert Valance/Legends|Beilert Valance]] arrived at [[Merl's]] to ask about [[Tyler Lucian]], a deserter from the Rebel Alliance, Glocken and the [[Gotal/Legends|Gotal]] enforcer [[Uri]] attempted to stop him from using force on their boss, but both were shot and killed by the intruder.<ref name="SW29" />

===In the shadows===
[[File:Boba_vs_Tayand_BT4.jpg|thumb|right|x150px|The Sakiyan crime lord Tayand spelled his own undoing by crossing Boba Fett.]]
{{Quote|You don't want to make an enemy of me, Fett!''"<br />"''No. You're a dangerous madman. I have no interest in having you as an enemy.|Tayand and Boba Fett, shortly before the latter kills the Sakiyan crime lord|<ref name="BT4">[[Blood Ties 4|''Blood Ties'' 4]]</ref>}}
Other Sakiyans became even more enmeshed in the galactic underworld as [[Scoundrel/Legends|scoundrels]],<ref name="UAA" /> outlaws, and members of criminal organizations. For instance, although the Sakiyan [[Tuden Sal]] was ostensibly the owner of a chain of restaurants during the latter years of the Galactic Republic, he maintained ties to several smuggling outfits as well. Lorn Pavan called in the favor with Tuden<ref name="DMSH 22">''[[Darth Maul: Shadow Hunter]]''</ref> in 32 BBY<ref name="NEC 73" />&mdash;the Human had previously provided key information that had helped the Sakiyan keep his liquor license&mdash;to ask Tuden to introduce him to criminal organizations, such as Black Sun, who could help him leave Coruscant and track down the Zabrak [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Sith Lord]] [[Darth Maul/Legends|Darth Maul]], who had information vital to the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]]. Tuden secured clearance codes to allow Pavan to leave the [[Capital/Legends|capital]] world, but the Sakiyan doubted the Human clerk's potential for success with a Sith awaiting him. Tuden kept I-5YQ,<ref name="DMSH 22" /> insisting he would deliver the droid to the [[Jedi Temple/Legends|Jedi Temple]] to deliver Pavan's critical information eventually,<ref name="CNIII" /> but he instead [[Memory wipe/Legends|wiped]] the droid's memory and kept the automaton for his personal bodyguard.<ref name="DMSH 22" /> Tuden went bankrupt soon thereafter when Senator Palpatine, via a proxy, initiated a hostile takeover of his business to help finance his plans to become [[Emperor/Legends|Emperor]]. Tuden thus became blacklisted by both the Empire and Black Sun. He lost his family and [[Tuden Sal's mate|mate]] in the process, and he was forced to sell I-5YQ and liquidate his other assets. With nowhere else to go, Tuden had joined the [[Whiplash]], an anti-Imperial organization on Coruscant<ref name="CNIII" /> by 19 BBY.<ref name="CN3 timeline">''[[Coruscant Nights III: Patterns of Force]]'' timeline</ref> As part of the group's leadership, Sal spearheaded a plan to assassinate the Galactic Emperor. The plot necessitated distracting other Whiplash leaders who thought the plan too risky, and it ultimately backfired, ending in Sal's death.<ref name="LJ" />

When the [[Togruta/Legends|Togruta]] [[Padawan/Legends|Padawan]] [[Ahsoka Tano/Legends|Ahsoka Tano]] lost her [[Ahsoka Tano's lightsabers/Legends|lightsaber]] on the planet Coruscant during the Clone Wars, she consulted a database of wanted criminals in the [[Jedi Archives/Legends|Jedi Archives]]; one of the profiles she considered as the possible thief was a Sakiyan.<ref name="LL">{{TCW|Lightsaber Lost}}</ref> During the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], a [[Unidentified Sakiyan smuggling ring|Sakiyan smuggling ring]] ran supplies for the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]] from a base in the [[Syvris shadowport]] near Hutt Space. Their routes ranged as far afield as the planets [[Corellia/Legends|Corellia]] and [[Terminus/Legends|Terminus]]. The operation came to the attention of the Galactic Empire shortly before the [[Battle of Hoth/Legends|Battle of Hoth]]<ref name="EGW" /> in [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]],<ref name="NEC 73" /> when [[Death Squadron/Legends|Death Squadron]], the personal [[Squadron/Legends|flight group]] of [[Darth/Legends|Darth]] Vader, enforcer for the Galactic Emperor, found the smugglers during a [[Raid on the Ulkantha asteroids|raid]] on the [[Ulkantha asteroids]]. With knowledge of their operation, the [[Chiss/Legends|Chiss]] [[Grand Admiral/Legends|Grand Admiral]] [[Mitth'raw'nuruodo/Legends|Thrawn]] formulated a strategy by which Vader would send Death Squadron against the smugglers' base in the Syvris [[Shadowport/Legends|shadowport]]. The [[Raid on Syvris shadowport|raid]] succeeded; Death Squadron nearly destroyed Syvris and gained custody of key members of the Sakiyan organization.<ref name="EGW" />

[[Tayand]] was a Sakiyan [[Crime lord/Legends|crime lord]] active during the Galactic Civil War, reputed for his insanity and bloodthirstiness.<ref name="BT2">[[Blood Ties 2|''Blood Ties'' 2]]</ref> When Tayand lost a large pot to the Human [[Connor Freeman]] in a game of [[Sabacc/Legends|sabacc]], he claimed that Freeman had cheated. The Human fled the scene, but Tayand put a bounty on his head.<ref name="BT4" /> The [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorian]] bounty hunter [[Boba Fett/Legends|Boba Fett]] pursued Freeman,<ref name="BT2" /> but another hunter, a Human named [[Daquinn]], reached the man first and brought him to [[Tayand's base]]<ref name="BT3">[[Blood Ties 3|''Blood Ties'' 3]]</ref> on the planet [[Cilare]]. Fett retook the bounty from Daquinn and his partner, the [[Whiphid/Legends|Whiphid]] [[Yarttar]]. However, when Fett tried to buy off Freeman's bounty to prevent him from being executed, Tayand refused. Freeman immediately offered a three-[[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|credit]] bounty for the Tayand, which created an excuse for Fett to kill the Sakiyan crime lord.<ref name="BT4" /> Another Sakiyan underworld figure during the Galactic Civil War was [[Torgas]], who headed an [[Assassin's Guild/Legends|Assassins' Guild]] on the planet [[Challon]]. The Empire contracted Torgas and his guild to assassinate [[Princess/Legends|Princess]] [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa]], a [[Senator/Legends|Senator]] from the planet [[Alderaan/Legends|Alderaan]], but the Human mercenary [[Giles Durane]] stymied the Sakiyan's plan after being hired by the young woman's [[Parent/Legends|father]], [[Bail Prestor Organa/Legends|Bail Organa]], to train her in weapons use.<ref name="TWM" /> When Torgas decided to take out Organa himself,<ref name="DOTA">{{StoryCite|story=Day of the Assassins!|book=Star Wars Weekly 105}}</ref> Durane killed him.<ref name="MESM" />
[[Naxy Screeger]] was a Sakiyan [[Gambling/Legends|gambling]] addict active during the [[Second Imperial Civil War]]. Naxy rarely found himself out of debt<ref name="CSWE III 131: NS" /> and was almost universally disliked, a condition exacerbated by his loquacious nature and poor command of Basic. On one occasion, Naxy skipped bail on the [[Feeorin/Legends|Feeorin]] [[Pirate/Legends|pirate]] [[Rav]], a move that brought him to the attention of the Human bounty hunter [[Cade Skywalker]] and his crew. They captured Naxy alongside a [[Bothan/Legends|Bothan]] Jedi named [[Hosk Trey'lis]] at [[Brogar's Safe House and Cantina]]<ref name="LECG" /> on the planet [[Lok/Legends|Lok]],<ref name="Leg23" /> then turned him in to Rav. Nevertheless, the Sakiyan talked his way out of captivity, and he even teamed up with Skywalker and his crew on their ship, the [[Mynock/Legends|''Mynock'']], on a mission to obtain the ''[[Grinning Liar]]'', a ship owned by a [[Wookiee/Legends|Wookiee]] smuggler named [[Chak (Wookiee)|Chak]].<ref name="LECG" /> In return for his help, Skywalker dropped Naxy off at the planet [[Socorro/Legends|Socorro]].<ref name="Leg23" /> Naxy drifted to the planet [[Kaer]], where he found work for the [[Houk/Legends|Houk]] criminal [[Lun Rask]];<ref name="Leg37">[[Legacy (2006) 37|''Legacy'' (2006) 37]]</ref> he then wound up working as the Hutt [[Vedo Anjiliac Atirue]]'s gatekeeper on the moon [[Nal Hutta/Legends|Nal Hutta]].<ref name="Leg49">[[Legacy (2006) 49|''Legacy'' (2006) 49]]</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|He's hard to spot in the cantina, but he's definitely there, with his gleaming black skin and inexpressive face.|Pablo Hidalgo, on the Sakiyan Djas Puhr's appearance in ''Star Wars'': Episode IV|<ref name="CRC 2" />}}
[[File:Cantina_masks_MOSW.jpg|thumb|left|x150px|The Sakiyan Djas Puhr was a character created for additional shots of the cantina for of ''A New Hope''.]]
[[Rick Baker]]'s special-effects team<ref name="SWOPM 12">[[Star Wars Official Poster Monthly 12|''Star Wars Official Poster Monthly'' 12]]</ref> created a bald, large-headed alien known as "Coal Man"<ref name="CRC 2" /> as a background character to be featured in the cantina sequence of [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']], first released in [[1977]]. The actor wearing the mask was part of supplemental shooting done in [[Wikipedia:Los Angeles|Los Angeles]], [[Wikipedia:California|California]], on [[January 24]] and [[January 25|25]], 1977.<ref name="MOSW">''[[The Making of Star Wars: The Definitive Story Behind the Original Film]]''</ref> When CBS television made ''[[The Star Wars Holiday Special]]'' in [[1978]], a pale-colored mask based on the same mold was used for the character Thorp.<ref name="CRC 2" />

The ''A New Hope'' character was first identified as Djas Puhr and his species as Sakiyan in [[1995]], when the character was featured on a card for [[Decipher]]'s [[Premiere Limited]] set, part of the [[Star Wars Customizable Card Game]]. The card also provides the earliest reference to the species' super-Human sensory powers.<ref name="CCG DP" /> Authors [[Steve Miller]] and [[Owen K.C. Stephens|Owen K. C. Stephens]] provided even greater detail about the species in ''[[Alien Anthology]]'', a [[2001]] supplement for [[Wizards of the Coast]]'s ''[[Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game]]'', which offers the Sakiyans as a species choice for characters created by players of the game.<ref name="AA" /> Author [[Michael Reaves]] fleshed out physiological and social aspects of the Sakiyans through characters featured in his [[MedStar Duology|''MedStar'' Duology]], published in [[2004]],<ref name="MS1" /><ref name="MS2">''[[MedStar II: Jedi Healer]]''</ref> and his [[Star Wars: Coruscant Nights|''Coruscant Nights'' trilogy]], published in [[2008]]<ref name="CNI">''[[Coruscant Nights I: Jedi Twilight]]''</ref><ref name="CNII">''[[Coruscant Nights II: Street of Shadows]]''</ref> and [[2009]].<ref name="CNIII" /> In the book ''[[The Making of Star Wars: The Definitive Story Behind the Original Film]]'', published in [[2007]], author [[Jonathan W. Rinzler]] confuses Djas Puhr with another large-headed cantina alien with his brain seemingly exposed. The second character, known as "Brain-guy" during filming,<ref name="MOSW" /> was later dubbed [[Pons Limbic/Legends|Pons Limbic]] and made a member of a separate species, the [[Siniteen/Legends|Siniteens]].<ref name="Hasbro PL">{{HasbroCite|set=Star Wars: The Legacy Collection|pack=#35: Pons Limbic|altlink=https://www.rebelscum.com/TLC35pons.asp}}</ref>

[[File:Thorp_in_the_cantina_SWHS.jpg|thumb|right|Thorp's mask in the ''Star Wars Holiday Special'' used the same mold as that of Djas Puhr in ''A New Hope''.]]
The various games that have featured Sakiyan characters have represented their unique abilities in disparate ways. The collectible card game version of Djas Puhr makes him more powerful after nightfall to reflect his advanced senses, for instance.<ref name="CCG DP" /> Sakiyan characters in ''Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game'' enjoy the ability to see in the dark, a bonus to sensory skills, fast reflexes, but a slightly lowered constitution.<ref name="AA" /> ''[[Ultimate Alien Anthology]]'', a revised and expanded version of the ''Alien Encounters'' sourcebook published in [[2003]], maintains the same general statistics for Sakiyan characters but also gives them bonuses to wilderness survival when the sense of smell can be used, does not lower their constitution, and gives them the ability to detect danger.<ref name="UAA" /> The ''[[Legacy Era Campaign Guide]]'', the iteration of the species written by [[Rodney Thompson]], [[Sterling Hershey]], and [[Gary Astleford]] and published in [[2009]] as an update to Wizards' [[Star Wars Roleplaying Game Saga Edition Core Rulebook|Saga Edition]] of the roleplaying game, allows Sakiyans to see in the dark but not to make out colors; it also gives them lightning-fast reflexes.<ref name="LECG" /> According to ''[[Alien Anthology]]'', most Sakiyans could speak Basic.<ref name="AA" /> However, the expanded version of that book, ''[[Ultimate Alien Anthology]]'', does not indicate that the language was common among the species.<ref name="UAA" /> The later book ''[[Legacy Era Campaign Guide]]'' grants all Sakiyans the language. This article follows the last source as the newest of the three.<ref name="LECG" /> The young-reader game books [[Episode I Adventures 6: The Hunt for Anakin Skywalker|''Episode I Adventures Game Book 6: The Hunt for Anakin Skywalker'']] and [[Episode I Adventures 7: Capture Arawynne|''Episode I Adventures Game Book 7: Capture Arawynne'']], both written by [[Dave Wolverton]] and published in [[2000]], allow readers to take on the role of the Sakiyan bounty hunter Djas Puhr. However, the novel versions of both stories attribute the actions in the game books to Sebulba, relegating the gamebooks to non-[[canon]]ical status.<ref name="HFAS">''[[Episode I Adventures 6: The Hunt for Anakin Skywalker]]''</ref><ref name="CA">''[[Episode I Adventures 7: Capture Arawynne]]''</ref> In the [[Star Wars video games|video game]] ''[[Star Wars: Yoda Stories]]'', first released in [[1997]], the Sakiyan Thorp is one of several characters who may spawn randomly during quests and interact with the player character.<ref name="YS">''[[Star Wars: Yoda Stories]]''</ref>
